cards.text: Israel just lost a battle to the Philistines (1 Samuel 4:10), and the Philistines captured the ark of God. Now they carry it from Ebenezer to Ashdod, one of their cities. I bet they think they just won the prize of the war, but friend, they have NO idea what they're holding.

cards.question: In Ashdod, the Philistines carry the ark into the temple of their god ___ and set it beside his statue.
The ark sits beside Dagon's statue all night. When the people of Ashdod get up early the next morning, what do they find?

answers.text: Dagon fallen on his face before the ark
The ark tipped over beside Dagon
Dagon's statue cracked down the middle

cards.question: After finding Dagon on his face, the people of Ashdod leave him lying there on the floor.

cards.text: They pick Dagon up and put him right back in his place. Friend, I dove face-first into the chocolate chips just last week, but at least I got back up BY MYSELF.

cards.question: The next morning, there's Dagon on his face before the ark of the LORD again. What's different this time?

answers.text: His head and hands are broken off
He is buried under the fallen roof

cards.text: Day one, Dagon falls down. Day two... he falls APART, with his head and hands lying on the threshold and only the torso left.

cards.question: Because of what happened, the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters his temple in Ashdod don't step on the threshold, even to this day.
Now the hand of the LORD is heavy on the people of Ashdod and the area around it. He ravages them and afflicts them with ___.
The men of Ashdod see what's happening to their city. What do they decide?

answers.text: The ark must not stay with them
Dagon must move to a new temple
They must bring more gifts to Dagon

cards.text: Their reason: "His hand is heavy upon us and upon our god Dagon." Friend, if I walked into my bakery two mornings in a row and found my oven face-down on the floor, I would NOT be waiting around for morning number three.

cards.question: The men of Ashdod call together all the rulers of the Philistines and ask what to do with the ark. Where do the rulers say to move it?
The ark moves to Gath, and the LORD's hand is against that city too, throwing it into great confusion. In Gath, only the old men get tumors.

cards.text: So they send the ark on to Ekron. Friend, this is a burning-hot cookie sheet and NOBODY has an oven mitt: pass it, pass it, PASS IT!

cards.question: The ark of the God of Israel arrives in Ekron. What do the Ekronites cry out?

answers.text: It was brought here to kill us
It will bring our city great honor
It belongs beside our own god now

cards.question: The Ekronites call together all the rulers of the Philistines. What do they want done with the ark?

answers.text: Send it back where it came from
Lock it away in Dagon's temple
Move it to the next Philistine city

cards.text: A deadly confusion fills Ekron, and the hand of God is very heavy on it. Those who don't die are afflicted with tumors.

cards.question: The people of Ekron cry out, and the outcry of the city goes up to ___.

cards.text: That's all for this batch, friend. But this ark's story? Still in the oven.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 3, 6, 9, 12 and 18 require unseen names, events or details that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Discovery questions therefore make up half of the stop's twelve choices, rather than just a few, and most choice cards are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card retells both Dagon's first fall in verse 3 and his second fall and damage in verse 4, but it cites only verse 4. Its citation should cover 1 Samuel 5:3-4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Move it to the next Philistine city" is not false anywhere in the passage. Moving the ark to another Philistine city is exactly what happens when it goes to Gath and then Ekron in verses 8-10.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
